title: Number Systems & Binary Conversion
summary: Digital computers utilize positional number systems including Binary (Base 2), Octal (Base 8), Decimal (Base 10), and Hexadecimal (Base 16).

images.title: Base Conversion Chart
images.caption: Positional values for Binary, Octal, Decimal, and Hexadecimal.

working_principle: Any number can be expressed as a summation of digits multiplied by radix powers: N = sum(d_i * r^i). In binary (r=2), each digit is a Bit (0 or 1). 4 bits form a Nibble, and 8 bits form a Byte.
boolean_equation: Decimal Value = d3·2³ + d2·2² + d1·2¹ + d0·2⁰
applications: Memory Address Decoding in Hexadecimal (0x00 to 0xFF)
Gray Code Encoders in Shaft Angle Optical Sensors
advantages: Binary aligns perfectly with ON/OFF transistor states
Hexadecimal provides compact 4-bit grouped human representation
disadvantages: BCD requires extra storage space compared to pure binary
common_mistakes: Forgetting to pad leading zeroes when converting binary to hex.
quick_notes: BCD represents each decimal digit (0-9) using 4 binary bits.
Gray code changes only ONE bit between consecutive numbers.

viva_questions.q: What is Gray Code and where is it used?
viva_questions.a: A non-weighted code where adjacent values differ by only 1 bit. Used in optical encoders to prevent error transitions.

viva_questions.q: Convert Decimal 12 to Binary and Hexadecimal.

interview_questions.q: Why is BCD used in digital displays instead of pure binary?
interview_questions.a: Because BCD maps directly decimal digits to 7-segment driver ICs (like 7447) without requiring complex division arithmetic.
